Since 1997, Canada has signed four major international climate commitments . It has met zero of them. Not Kyoto. Not Copenhagen. Not Paris. And the legislated Net Zero by 2050 target has no credible pathway to achievement according to the government's own Environment Commissioner. Meanwhile, total federal climate-related spending since 2015 has exceeded $100 billion — and emissions have barely…

Canada's Paris Agreement target is 40–45% below 2005 levels by 2030 , which means emissions must fall to approximately 401–438 Mt CO₂e . As of 2022, emissions stood at roughly 670 Mt — meaning Canada must eliminate 232–269 Mt in under six years . That is more than the entire emissions output of the oil sands.
